messages.author: 01cd8de9535fc3d1
messages.subject: confused about alpha
parts:
I'm confused about how the alpha aesthetic works in geom_rect.

Consider the following:
=====================================
plot.df <- data.frame(a = 0, b = 0)
rectangles.df <- data.frame(
a = 0,
b = 0,
ymin = c(0, 2, 4, 0, 2, 4),
ymax = c(2, 4, 6, 2, 4, 6),
xmin = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
xmax = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2),
transparency = c(1, 128, 256, 32, 64, 96))
ggplot(data = plot.df, aes(x = a, y = b)) +
geom_rect(
data = rectangles.df,
aes(
xmin = xmin,
xmax = xmax,
ymin = ymin,
ymax = ymax,
alpha = 1/transparency),
fill = "red") +
opts(legend.position = "none")
======================================

I expected to get six red rectangles, each with a different alpha. Instead, I got one opaque rectangle and five rectangles with the same transparency.

Anyone know what's going on here?

David

messages.subject: Re: confused about alpha

Probably 1/32 = 0.03 is too low to arise into visual awareness, hence
all but alpha 1/1 fails to enter our awareness.
Try this transparency:

transparency = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6))

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: confused about alpha
parts:
Hi,

The previous post was incorrect.
ggplot2 uses scale system for alpha, and by default, the alpha is
mapped to the range of 0.1-1.0.
see ?scale_alpha

This means that your transparency: 1/c(1, 128, 256, 32, 64, 96)
is mapped to the value: 1.0000000 0.1035294 0.1000000 0.1247059
0.1105882 0.1058824

The difference among 1/32, 1/64, etc is very very small, which fails
to enter our visual awareness.

--
Kohske Takahashi <takahash...@gmail.com>

messages.subject: Re: confused about alpha
parts:
Kohske,

Thanks for clarifying that.

So to keep transparency from being mapped to scale_alpha, I need to make it a factor:
====================================

plot.df <- data.frame(a = 0, b = 0)
rectangles.df <- data.frame(
a = 0,
b = 0,
ymin = c(0, 2, 4, 0, 2, 4),
ymax = c(2, 4, 6, 2, 4, 6),
xmin = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
xmax = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2),
transparency = factor(c(1, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.1)))

ggplot(data = plot.df, aes(x = a, y = b)) +
geom_rect(
data = rectangles.df,
aes(
xmin = xmin,
xmax = xmax,
ymin = ymin,
ymax = ymax,
alpha = transparency),

fill = "red") +
opts(legend.position = "none")
====================================

Just what I wanted.

David
